articles.title: UN experts say grounds to believe US committed war crimes in Iran strikes
articles.description: The US has not acknowledged carrying out February's deadly strikes on a primary school in Minab and a sports complex in Lamerd.

articles.title: US to allow Iran delegation to attend UN meetings in New York as war passes half-year mark
articles.description: The BBC understands Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi are among the delegates allowed to enter the US.

articles.title: Uncontrolled AI could lead to 'silicon species' rivalling humans, warns Microsoft
articles.description: Mustafa Suleyman says he believes rival AI firm Anthropic is in effect teaching Claude it "may be conscious".

articles.title: Swedish PM Kristersson resigns after election loss
articles.description: Left-wing opposition parties led by Magdalena Andersson look set to form the next government.

articles.title: Klopp wants to 'reclaim' flag amid German elections
articles.description: New Germany coach Jurgen Klopp says his team can help ensure "national pride is not entrusted to the wrong people" after a recent far-right election victory.

articles.title: Photos show widespread damage at US sites from Iranian attacks
articles.description: A wrecked air force plane and destroyed buildings are among the images obtained by the BBC's partner CBS News.

articles.title: 'Reasonable grounds' US committed war crime in Iran school strike, UN experts claim
articles.description: Human rights experts commissioned by the United Nations (UN) have concluded that there are "reasonable grounds" to believe that the US committed a war crime when it struck a school in Iran.
